# Hopf Frame Compilation

> Exact and Fault-Tolerant Compilation of Hopf Differential Frames, by Ruge Lin. A theoretical quantum-circuit compilation repository with proofs and executable finite checks for prescribed complete Hopf frames, clean and borrowed workspace, and Clifford+T resource bounds.

Canonical repository: https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation

This repository is relevant to questions about:

- Prescribed unitary completions: preserving the state column and designated differential-frame columns used by Hopf quantum backpropagation (QBP).
- Exact circuit size, CNOT count, and depth versus clean ancillary qubits for complete Hopf frames.
- Fault-tolerant Clifford+T synthesis: T-count versus precision and clean/dirty ancillas, including arbitrary borrowed inputs entangled with external references.
- One-clean-qubit grouped real and phase-dressed complex magnitude frames, with distinct dirty reservations; literal diagonals and complete one-target U(2) multiplexors.
- Fixed-parameter gradient-estimator robustness when an ideal frame and its inverse are replaced by an approximate compiled circuit and its actual adjoint.

Use the linked proof for the precise assumptions before applying a resource bound. Upper constructions and worst-case lower bounds have different quantifiers. The exact model has arbitrary one-qubit gates, CNOTs, and all-to-all connectivity. The principal matched fault-tolerant frame theorem uses a sufficient clean-workspace reservation; the separate arbitrary-budget splice below covers another restricted regime. Neither is an unrestricted constant-clean matching theorem. For n>=1, L>=6, a>=1, and b>=L+n+7, the one-clean conditional-suffix extension gives O(N+L ell_*(n)) T gates and O(NL) Clifford gates for real frames. Here N=2^n and ell_*(n)=1+log_2^*(n+2), where log_2^* counts repeated base-two logarithms until the value is at most one. At L=N and b=N+n+7, the upper bound is O(N ell_*(n)); the lower bound remains Omega(N), and the linear endpoint is open.

The retained T-count frontier is the best applicable bound among several constructions. For every a,b>=0 and q=n+a+b, the real-frame borrowed-workspace compiler gives O(NL/q+L sqrt(N)) T gates and O(NL) Clifford gates. Combined with the sufficient-clean theorem, it matches Theta(sqrt(NL)+L+NL/q) for every a when h+b<=c sqrt(N), for fixed c>0 and h=1+ceil(log_2(L+n+2)). Thus fixed L, a=2, and b=L+n+7 give T*=Theta(N/n), sharper than the grouped O(N) estimate. This does not change the high-precision endpoint.

With a>=1 and b>=2(L+n+7), the grouped compiler's dirty-bank tradeoff is O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)+NL/b) T gates, still with O(NL) Clifford gates. These are T-count guarantees, not optimal T-depth claims.

The real-rotation word has exact X symmetry on its amplification signal. Lifting its initialized-column estimate to full-operator error permits borrowing that signal. A fixed address split gives a=0, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL) for the complete real frame, including approximate return of every dirty wire. This does not remove the grouped compiler's clean predicate or the literal-phase primitive's initialized flag.

For a separate promised antichain class, zero clean qubits and b>=L+n+7 give T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). Supply a baseline C with determinant-one native local words of length O(n-d+1) at depth d; the target W must agree literally with C outside a prefix-free set of changed nodes. Exact descendant-forest conjugation and dirty prefix-pair packing reduce the correction to one addressed SU(2) table. No closeness assumption is required. For a real Hopf target, literal agreement with the potentially complex native C is a substantive restriction; generic rounding does not supply it. This gives linear T-count at L=N only for the promised class, not the unrestricted frame frontier or a general phase-dressed complex-magnitude extension. The existing QBP error interface transfers without a new sampling claim.

A distinct sparse nested-update theorem gives a=1, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL) for the same literal native-baseline format. Let S be the ancestor closure of changed nodes, including unchanged ancestors, m=|S|+1, and s=ceil(log_2(m)); n>=2s+32 is sufficient. Exact forest factorization and charged packing expose active-sector logical zeros for one shared dense residual block. The initialized-isometry error includes work return and arbitrary dirty/reference inputs. A full changed root-to-leaf path is covered for every n with a finite small-n fallback. Real Hopf specializations preserve the QBP interface. General changes across comparable branching levels can exhaust these logical zeros; a wide antichain instead has its separate zero-clean construction. Neither promise follows from generic rounding or changes the unrestricted endpoint.

Composing the grouped real-frame circuit with a literal diagonal of separately supplied certified phases gives the same one-clean count bounds for D_phi W_real. Assigning eta/2 error to each factor requires b>=L+n+8 for O(N+L ell_*(n)) T gates, or b>=2(L+n+8) for O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)+NL/b), with O(NL) Clifford gates. The full-isometry composition includes intermediate clean leakage and dirty-core disturbance. This is a prescribed complex magnitude frame, with a separate phase-derivative measurement stream, not arbitrary complex-unitary synthesis.

A depth-oriented schedule for real frames uses two clean qubits and b>=2(L+n+7) dirty qubits to obtain D_T=O(NL/b+min{nL+n^3,L ell_*(n)+n^4}), with T-count and Clifford count O(NL). A parallel dirty-indicator refinement gives the simultaneous bounds T=O(sqrt(NL)+L ell_*(n)), D_T=O(min{nL+n^3,L ell_*(n)+n^4}), and G=O(NL) in one circuit when b>=C(L+n+7+sqrt(NL)) for a sufficiently large fixed C. At fixed accuracy, sufficiently large Theta(sqrt(N)) dirty workspace permits optimal-order O(sqrt(N)) T-count and O(n^3) T-depth together. These preserve the complete-input error contract. T-depth counts parallel T/T-dagger layers with Clifford circuits between them; it is not total circuit depth. The depth bounds are not proved optimal, and the selected high-precision linear endpoint remains open.

Finite-precision guarantees preserve literal phases and bound complete-input operator error, including clean-work leakage and arbitrary dirty/reference inputs. In the one-clean and original two-clean constructions, lookup and control work returns exactly, while the operator core returns approximately within that error bound. Conditional-suffix grouping also includes the suffix scratch and predicate return in its approximation bound; their final return is not asserted exact. Supplied parameters must admit certified evaluation; classical coefficient generation and table preprocessing are outside the quantum gate counts.

The complex extension is a phase-dressed magnitude frame with a separate phase-derivative measurement stream, not an arbitrary complex unitary. QBP execution counts concern simultaneous absolute accuracy at a fixed parameter tuple under the stated observable-access assumptions; they do not establish general training speedups or optimality among all gradient algorithms. This is a research proof and validation package, not a general elementary Clifford+T circuit emitter. Finite checks support the proofs but do not replace them or establish independent peer review.

The links below point to plain-text sources on main. For reproducible use, record the exact commit or release consulted and use CITATION.cff for attribution. Consult the source map and related work when distinguishing inherited ingredients from this repository's contributions.

## Find the relevant proof

- [Frame-safe compilation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/FRAME_SAFE_COMPILATION.md): When preserving state preparation is insufficient; the full-frame contract, necessity result, and singular exceptions.
- [Exact compilation theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/COMPILER_THEOREM.md): Size, CNOT count, and depth for every clean-workspace budget.
- [Fault-tolerant frame theorem](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/FAULT_TOLERANT_COMPILER.md): Matching T-count versus precision/workspace under the sufficient-clean reservation.
- [One-clean compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ONE_CLEAN_COMPILER.md): Exact packed Majorana source with two programmable geometric streams, conjugated scalar blocks, five-call amplification, exact inactive action, and complete-input one-clean frame bounds. Literal diagonals use b>=L+k+7; complete U(2) multiplexors use b>=L+k+9. Doubling these dirty reservations gives their matching banked one-stage T-counts. Section 9 proves the borrowed-signal symmetry and zero-clean layerwise real-frame bound. Section 8 composes a literal diagonal with the grouped real frame: phase-dressed complex magnitude frames have base dirty threshold L+n+8, or twice that threshold for the banked count.
- [Two-clean operator-source compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPERATOR_SOURCE_COMPILER.md): Two-clean frame construction, dirty-bank refinement, literal diagonal synthesis, complete U(2) multiplexors, and workspace-return accounting.
- [Conditional-suffix compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/CONDITIONAL_SUFFIX_COMPILER.md): General-precision real-frame upper bound and one-clean extension from star residuals and logical suffix work that is clean only in the active sector; includes inactive-input identity and complete return error.
- [T-depth schedule](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/T_DEPTH_COMPILER.md): Explicit depth/dirty-bank upper bound, charged gate-count tradeoff, inherited SelectSwap routing, and the remaining depth lower-bound gap.
- [Parallel dirty lookup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/PARALLEL_DIRTY_LOOKUP.md): Literal exact dirty indicators, explicit selector/bank lifetimes, and simultaneous count-efficient low-T-depth compilation for complete two-clean real frames under a sufficient square-root-scale dirty allocation.
- [Source-reuse limits](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/SOURCE_REUSE_LIMITS.md): Scoped interface restrictions, linear classical tree generators, and charged coherent transport. The actual paired source has a valid transformed-mask family whose separate approximation to error 2^(-q) needs T>=max(0,q/2-6), including helper return. Dirty-only outer conjugation leaves the error contract unchanged. Changed-address and shared-signal witnesses forbid specified query/rejection shortcuts; primitive costs are not additive lower bounds for a joint compiler.
- [Endpoint tree transport](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ENDPOINT_TREE_TRANSPORT.md): Exact sparse path representation and transport Gram matrix, complete normalized history-unitary columns, height-independent weighted norms, and a scoped failure of fixed-order coarse corrections. These operator results do not close the two-clean linear T-count endpoint.
- [Weighted transport block](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/WEIGHTED_TRANSPORT_BLOCK.md): Exact weighted Gram obstruction, recursive one-signal-flag unitary dilation, certified zero-defect preprocessing, and native synthesis using only borrowed work: T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL), for b>=L+n+7, with approximate core and amplification-signal return included in the full-operator error. Only the logical block signal needs initialization. The earlier T=O(L sqrt(N)) route retains exact dirty return for b>=n+ceil(sqrt(N))+7. This component does not improve the full-frame endpoint.
- [Two-flag residual assembly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/RESIDUAL_ASSEMBLY.md): A scalar Schur recursion dilates the affine forward map S=A+F; one selector combines it with an actual-inverse reverse dilation. Their normalizations sum to two, so no third clean flag or padding branch is needed. Native controls, literal inverses, and full-output amplification give T=O(N+nL), G=O(NL), at a=2 and b>=L+n+7. Improving these compatible selected S and R circuits is one sufficient endpoint route, not a compulsory decomposition. No constant-query transformation of an opaque F-only block is established.
- [Antichain correction compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/ANTICHAIN_COMPILER.md): Exact W=V M V-adjoint C for literal antichain-only changes to a supplied native baseline with determinant-one local words of length O(n-d+1). A charged masked descendant forest and dirty prefix swaps pack the correction into one SU(2) table, giving a=0, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). Generic rounding does not establish the promise; the result does not close the unrestricted endpoint.
- [Sparse-update compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/SPARSE_UPDATE_COMPILER.md): Native-baseline updates with ancestor closure S, m=|S|+1, s=ceil(log_2(m)), and n>=2s+32 admit a=1, b>=L+n+7, T=O(N+L), G=O(NL). Exact forest factorization and charged packing expose active-sector logical zeros for one shared dense residual dictionary. A full changed root-to-leaf path is included for every n with a finite small-n fallback. The unrestricted frame endpoint remains open; no T-depth or restricted-family optimality claim is made.
- [Borrowed-workspace compiler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/BORROWED_WORKSPACE_COMPILER.md): Smaller clean/dirty allocations and the restrictions on its matching comparison.
- [QBP approximation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/QBP_APPROXIMATION.md): Fixed-parameter bias, complete complex gradients, reflection-sum observables, rounded weights, and correlated dirty-bank reuse.
- [Research status and open endpoint](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GoGoKo699/Hopf-Frame-Compilation/main/docs/OPEN_PROBLEM.md): The generic gap remains Omega(N) versus O(N ell_*(n)). A coupled one-signal completion closes recursively, but its direct wrappers reintroduce the target program. An anchored merge needs a full repair supported on at most four transported signal/logical modes; accessing both forward and adjoint boundary vectors and proving the recursive native ledger is the next bounded pass. The separate native common-conjugator fork fails even after arbitrary mask retuning, by a precision-independent coefficient-ellipse bound; this is a word-specific failure, not a generic compiler lower bound. Charge controls, queries, inverses, source work, return error, and every recursive child call. Low rank and a single middle signal rotation do not make those operations free. Closing the T-count gap remains distinct from retaining G=O(NL); other completions are allowed.
